invariants.description: exact solution: q_vc_Na = q_vc_Na_init + (v_giEpi_NKE + v_lptEpi_NKE + v_rptEpi_NKE - v_lgl_Na - v_rgl_Na) t (sodium mass balance of the circulation)
invariants.expr: np.max(np.abs(q_vc_Na - (q_vc_Na_init + (v_giEpi_NKE + v_lptEpi_NKE + v_rptEpi_NKE - v_lgl_Na - v_rgl_Na)*t))) <= 1e-9*max(1.0e-3, np.max(np.abs(q_vc_Na)))

bc_sweep.rationale: Na_circ is a pure integrator, so any finite constant fluxes work; the ranges span the magnitudes the fluxes take in the source model (glomerular Na flux about 3.5e-3 mol/s per kidney with kK_gl_Na = 1 /s; NKE fluxes of either sign, since the simplified NKE runs backwards when the gradients reverse), and q_vc_Na_init spans 1 mmol to 1 mol (source-model value 11.5 mmol; a physiological extracellular Na pool is about 2 mol). q_vc_Na may become negative for draining fluxes over long runs; that is not claimed as an invariant because the component itself has no positivity constraint.

baseline.reason: a pure sodium integrator (mass balance) with no physiological counterpart on its own; it is verified against its exact solution. Whole-body sodium-balance data (e.g. plasma Na with changes in intake) belong to a network using BVC_GI, BVC_Kidney and BVC_Na_circ together.

calibrate.note: not_applicable: no free rate parameters: the only constant is the initial Na content, which is an initial condition, not a behaviour to calibrate.
